forces.title: Retail Shift to Ecosystem-based Platform Models
forces.description: The retail industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation, moving from traditional transaction-centric operations to relationship-centric, ecosystem-based platform models. Competitive advantage is increasingly derived from orchestrating interconnected networks of consumers, brands, logistics, and AI services, rather than just product assortment or physical footprint. This shift enables retailers to generate multiple revenue streams beyond merchandise sales, such as retail media and embedded financial services, driving self-sustaining growth through network effects.
forces.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

forces.title: Accelerated AI Adoption Driving Retail Productivity and ROI
forces.description: AI is no longer a niche technology but a central pillar of growth for consumer and retail businesses, with 74% of organizations expecting to deploy AI at scale within 12 months. This widespread adoption is enhancing productivity by 35-37% by 2030, delivering measurable ROI across operations, from demand forecasting and dynamic pricing to inventory management and supply chain optimization. AI augments human capabilities, allowing retailers to manage complexity, scale revenue faster than costs, and elevate customer experiences through hyper-personalization, despite cost pressures.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

forces.title: K-shaped Consumer Spending Creating Income-Based Retail Divergence
forces.description: Financial pressure is reshaping consumer spending, leading to a 'K-shaped economy' where higher-income households continue to spend while lower-income groups struggle. Retailers can no longer rely on traditional essential/discretionary or premium/value labels. They must adopt cohort-intelligent strategies, fortifying 'good-better-best' product ranges, deploying targeted pricing and promotions, and redesigning loyalty programs. This divergence creates opportunities for growth on both sides of the income gap by tailoring offerings to specific customer priorities and channel preferences, navigating shifts in demand category by category.
forces.source_title: Consumer Spending in Canada Is Shifting, Just Not How You’d Expect

forces.title: Rapid Growth of E-commerce and Quick Commerce
forces.description: India’s e-commerce market is experiencing phenomenal growth, projected to reach US$345 billion by 2030, driven by rapid digital adoption and increasing disposable incomes. Quick commerce, in particular, has emerged as a US$7-8 billion market in FY25, growing at a CAGR of 110-130% (2021-25) and expected to reach US$65-70 billion by 2030. This growth is fueled by high-frequency, convenience-led consumption, especially in Tier II and III cities, where online shoppers are expanding rapidly. E-commerce platforms like Amazon and Flipkart are investing heavily in infrastructure and seller support.

forces.title: Tier 2/3 Cities Driving Significant Incremental E-commerce Demand
forces.description: Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities are emerging as critical growth engines for India’s e-commerce sector, contributing over 60% of total e-commerce demand and 50% of incremental orders in 2025. Despite lower internet user penetration (25-30% compared to metros' 45-50%), these cities are at the forefront of digital payments adoption and consumption. Government initiatives and infrastructure development in these regions further position them as key drivers of future economic growth and retail expansion, fostering demand for both online and organized retail.

forces.title: AI-Driven Portfolio Management for Physical Retail Networks
forces.description: Retailers are increasingly adopting an AI-driven portfolio approach to manage their store networks, moving beyond traditional four-wall profit and loss (P&L) metrics. AI enables real-time decisions on pricing, labor, and inventory, transforming store operations from scheduled routines to continuously optimized actions. Stores are now viewed as infrastructure supporting broader ecosystems, acting as fulfillment hubs, brand amplifiers, and data generation nodes. This strategy optimizes for role, resilience, and ecosystem value, allowing for strategic investments in locations that contribute to network-level advantages like delivery speed or retail media reach.
forces.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

forces.title: Strong Policy Support and FDI for Retail Growth
forces.description: India's retail sector benefits significantly from supportive government policies, including 100% FDI permitted in B2B and marketplace e-commerce models. Initiatives like the National Logistics Policy aim to improve supply chain efficiency and cost-effectiveness, while the 'Digital India' campaign targets a trillion-dollar online economy by 2025. Reduced GST for select categories, personal income tax relief, and lower lending rates further boost private consumption. This policy framework, combined with increasing FDI, creates a conducive environment for retail expansion and modernization, attracting substantial international investment.

forces.title: Digital Payments and Public Infrastructure Boosting Retail
forces.description: India’s rapidly expanding digital payments landscape, particularly UPI, is a significant tailwind for the retail sector. UPI processed 22.35 billion transactions in April 2026, becoming the world's largest retail fast payment system by volume. This, combined with Digital Public Infrastructure like Aadhaar and Account Aggregator, provides seamless, secure transaction capabilities that are vital for both online and offline retail growth. Increased payment penetration and convenience encourage consumer spending and accelerate the shift towards digital commerce, reducing friction in transactions.

forces.title: New Revenue Streams from Retail Media and Embedded Finance
forces.description: Leading global retailers are increasingly diversifying revenue streams beyond traditional merchandise sales, generating significant income from retail media, digital advertising, embedded financial services, and marketplace commissions. These adjacent revenue streams often offer stronger margins and simultaneously enhance customer engagement. This focus on creating multiple engines of value across the ecosystem, driven by data-driven business insights and loyalty programs, strengthens the overall profitability and competitive position of retailers, moving towards a broader value proposition.
forces.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

forces.title: Data Foundations and Governance Critical for AI-driven Retail
forces.description: For AI to be effective in retail, strengthening data foundations and governance is paramount. Much of retailers' rich operational and customer data remains siloed, leading to blind spots and reliance on instinct over insight. Executives recognize data as the second highest area for increased investment, after cybersecurity. Focus on data security, powered forecasting, and analysis is critical. Establishing clear governance, ethics, and decision-making processes, along with retaining human oversight, is crucial for maintaining customer trust and effectively leveraging AI for personalization and service improvement.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

forces.title: Growing Demand for Personalized Customer Experiences
forces.description: As consumers become increasingly digital-savvy, there is a growing demand for enhanced personalized experiences across retail channels. Agentic AI, capable of autonomous decisions and continuous learning, holds the potential to automate end-to-end trade flows and deliver hyper-personalized experiences. Retailers are focusing on leveraging data from e-commerce, CRM, loyalty programs, and social media to build a comprehensive customer-centric view. This personalization is vital for driving customer engagement, improving brand loyalty, and converting consideration into purchase, leading to higher revenue.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

forces.title: Streamlined Supply Chains and Advanced Logistics Infrastructure
forces.description: Improvements in supply chain and logistics are a significant tailwind for retailers. An interoperable digital layer can streamline the supply chain by connecting manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, enabling seamless payments, financing, and reconciliation. Retailers are integrating AI into delivery coverage, route density, and click-and-collect throughput, partnering with logistics providers for automated warehouses. Government initiatives like the National Logistics Policy aim to further smoothen deliveries to hinterlands, making logistics efficient and cost-effective, directly improving operational efficiency and customer satisfaction for retailers.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: High Inflation and Stretched Household Budgets Pressuring Consumer Spend
forces.description: Canadian parents expect to spend nearly $700 on back-to-school items, with rising prices being the main driver, not bigger baskets. Over half of parents struggle to fit this spending into their normal household budgets, particularly lower and middle-income families. This pattern reflects broader consumer spending trends where the Top-20% pull away while others rely on savings and debt. Retailers face the challenge of attracting price-sensitive consumers who may cut dining out, entertainment, and non-school clothing to protect essential purchases, demanding value-focused propositions.
forces.source_title: What Back-to-School Tells Retailers About the Seasons Ahead

viewpoints.title: India Retail Sector Poised to Become World's Third Largest by 2030
viewpoints.description: India's retail sector is on a strong growth trajectory, expected to exceed US$2.36 trillion by 2030, making it the world's third-largest. This expansion is supported by government initiatives to boost disposable incomes and consumption, combined with the country's large population, growing middle-income class, and increasing urbanization. The sector offers highly favorable investment opportunities for multinational corporations due to its wealth of resources, affordable labor, and attractive tax breaks, driving robust investor interest and market expansion.

viewpoints.title: Retail Reinventing Business Model to Relationship-Centric, Ecosystem-Driven Platforms
viewpoints.description: Retail is undergoing a fundamental reinvention, shifting from a transaction-centric model to a relationship-centric one, and from optimizing individual channels to orchestrating interconnected ecosystems. Competitive advantage is now built on bringing together consumers, brands, sellers, logistics, financial institutions, and AI-powered services into integrated platforms. This creates multiple engines of value beyond traditional commerce, including customer engagement, data, services, and partnerships, driving self-sustaining growth through network effects that are difficult to replicate.
viewpoints.source_title: From commerce to platform : Reimagining retail as an intelligent ecosystem

viewpoints.title: AI Central to Retail Growth and Competitiveness, Augmenting Human Capabilities
viewpoints.description: AI is no longer a niche technology but the central pillar of future growth and competitiveness in the consumer and retail sector. Executives are rapidly integrating AI into core workflows, expecting to deploy it at scale. AI is seen as a powerful engine to create new value by boosting productivity, achieving sharper demand forecasting, honing dynamic pricing, and streamlining supply chains. It augments human capabilities, allowing revenue to scale faster than costs and transforming employees to higher-value advisory roles, driving sustainable performance.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Consumer & Retail

viewpoints.title: India's E-commerce Entering High-Growth Phase Driven by Digital Adoption, Tier-2/3 Demand
viewpoints.description: India's e-commerce industry is experiencing a high-growth phase, fueled by increasing digital adoption and evolving consumer behavior. Key drivers include rising disposable incomes, robust demand from Tier II & III cities, and a significant surge in quick commerce. The market is projected to reach US$345 billion by 2030, with D2C brands also expanding rapidly. Government initiatives, infrastructure development, and growing internet penetration further underscore the sector's potential for sustained, strong growth across urban and rural regions.

viewpoints.title: Retailers Must Adopt Portfolio Approach to Store Management with AI Integration
viewpoints.description: Retailers need to evolve from traditional store-level P&L metrics to a portfolio approach, recognizing the broader value individual locations contribute to the entire network. AI has made it feasible to manage stores as infrastructure supporting the ecosystem, fulfillment hubs, and digital engagement nodes. This requires defining distinct roles for stores, designing for resilience against market volatility, and measuring ecosystem value beyond direct margins. Companies that optimize their store networks with AI will gain a durable competitive advantage and capture growth in dynamic retail environments.
viewpoints.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

viewpoints.title: Shifting Consumer Spending Demands Cohort-Intelligent Retail Strategies Amid K-shaped Economy
viewpoints.description: Canadian consumer spending is undergoing significant shifts, creating a 'K-shaped economy' where resilience in retail categories defies traditional labels. As household budgets tighten, consumers are making unpredictable cuts, protecting some discretionary spending while reducing others. Retailers must identify their offerings' positioning within this new budget hierarchy, tailoring strategies to specific income cohorts. This requires fortifying range architecture (good-better-best), deploying cohort-intelligent pricing and promotions, redesigning loyalty programs, and capitalizing on channel preferences to own growth amidst diverging demand patterns.
viewpoints.source_title: Consumer Spending in Canada Is Shifting, Just Not How You’d Expect

viewpoints.title: Interoperable Digital Layer Crucial for Streamlining B2B Supply Chains in Retail
viewpoints.description: An interoperable digital layer is identified as a key force multiplier for India's business sector, including its impact on retailing. This layer can significantly streamline the supply chain by securely connecting manufacturers, distributors, and retailers. It enables seamless payments, financing, and reconciliation across the entire ecosystem, addressing friction caused by information asymmetry and manual operations. This digital infrastructure is vital for improving transactional efficiency and credit access, ultimately helping retailers and their partners grow.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit
